# Kerr Phase Query Thresholds

This repository classifies the number of identical forward Kerr-gate uses
needed for globally consistent calibration of the nonlinear phase. The
complete scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, threshold table, finite separation,
  reading route, reproduction command, purpose and contact.
- science/model.md: gate, target and nuisance, query count, peak occupation
  versus total construction cap, error definitions, exact R1/R2/R3 and S1/S2/S3.
- science/query_thresholds.md: adaptive history support and the phase-risk
  lemma; exact Haar floors; three-triangular and fixed-total four-mode bands;
  exact exposed-photon parity refinement.
- science/global_confidence.md: cyclic residue bound, inert-prime omissions,
  uniform shrinking-window converse, fixed joint absolutely continuous priors,
  heralding, and achievable confidence at the threshold.
- science/timing_and_priors.md: finite positive commensurate duration catalog;
  qualitative iff criterion for an improving linear-phase prior; separate
  sufficient and necessary confidence/RMS rates and their nonmatching gap.
- science/coherent_preparation.md: sine state, reversible arithmetic,
  fixed-point search without QRAM, work-register error bound, and the
  separately assumed coherent number-to-Fock loading interface.
- science/four_photon_protocol.md: four code words and amplitudes, selected
  pair preparation, echoed middle edge, finite Fourier readout and exact risk.
- science/robustness.md: independent cubic phase, converse simulation,
  finite-witness tolerance and conservative asymptotic sufficient tolerance.
- science/access_variants.md: one shortened Hamiltonian call and a
  forward/inverse pair, with bypass photons and changed access assumptions.
- science/ising_application.md: one fixed-time all-to-all Ising interrogation,
  all-input converse, parity spectra, fixed real prior and scope.
- science/interpretation.md: physical connections, local/global distinction,
  common nuisance, resources and established boundaries.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: imported ingredients, exact source pointers,
  nearby models and actual limits of the literature comparison.
- references/references.bib: structured source metadata.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: the shared 30-milestone sequence, with 14 background
  milestones and 16 narrative and innovation milestones; prerequisites,
  understanding targets, conceptual connections and canonical pointers.
- learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md: selected sections of Watrous's 2018 author
  manuscript, notation conventions, finite-register and phase-estimation
  connections, a complete four-photon example, and project-specific bridges.
- verification/README.md: commands, dependencies, expected outputs and scope.
- verification/run_all.py: reproducible finite-check runner.

Reader routes:
- For the scientific story: model, query thresholds, global confidence,
  interpretation; follow the relevant constructive or access page.
- For an exact theorem: use the authoritative statement and full proof,
  together with its named resource conditions and cited ingredients.
- For an implementation ingredient: read coherent preparation or the finite
  protocol, then its verification and explicit control assumptions.
- For the shared learning route: use learning/MILESTONES.md and its source
  bridge. M01-M14 assemble the background and complete operational model;
  M15-M30 assemble the research arguments and their global synthesis.
  Both phases proceed from local ingredients to the complete story.
- To reproduce: use verification/README.md and run the current scripts;
  distinguish present execution from a historical report.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- Watrous's The Theory of Quantum Information is the single educational
  anchor. Its section/page pointers refer to the standard-layout 2018
  author manuscript. Primary research citations supply the separate
  phase-estimation, arithmetic, algorithmic and control ingredients.
- The learning map is project-defined and shared by all readers. Its
  milestones point to the authoritative science; they do not replace proofs.
- Watrous's trace distance is the unhalved trace norm, and its fidelity is
  unsquared. State the convention when translating a measurement-error bound.
- Finite-dimensional quantum-register results apply at each fixed cutoff.
  POVM normalization on a code must be completed on the full physical space.
- q counts all unknown-gate uses per complete estimate, including repeated
  probes and sensing attempts. Auxiliary preparation before any query has
  a separate control cost.
- The same unknown beta acts on every call. Independent per-call Haar
  linear phases define a different, theta-independent averaged channel.
- Adaptive lower bounds allow arbitrary ancillas and controls under a
  hard per-query occupation cap. Upper bounds use a stricter total photon
  cap including the explicitly specified bypass reference.
- A sequential history's sum n_j is cumulative linear exposure, not
  automatically the initial photon count.
- Constant exact risk floors and matching optimal risk exponents use Haar
  priors. Achievable O(N^-4) risk is pointwise in both phases.
- The subthreshold confidence theorem holds for every fixed joint AC prior,
  even narrow or correlated densities; it does not cover singular or
  N-dependent concentrating priors.
- A constant N^-2 window gives a fixed-confidence guarantee. Confidence
  tends to one for delta_N -> 0 with N^2 delta_N -> infinity.
- The original four-use achievability chooses an odd exposed total at most
  N. Exactly N exposed photons for every parity is a different promise.
  Its five-use necessity concerns vanishing Haar risk / full-circle minimax
  consistency. Four uses can be consistent at even exact totals on a known
  target interval of width less than pi/2, using a band with spacing four.
- The finite positive duration catalog and its clock step are fixed in N.
  The exact four-use upper bound refers to the original primitive gate.
- w_N -> 0 is the sharp qualitative three-use calibration criterion for a
  fixed AC theta prior and an independent uniform beta interval of known
  center. Quantitative sufficient and necessary rate bounds do not match.
- Coherent arithmetic costs O(N polylog N), not polylog N. A separate Fock
  loader and nonlinear calibrated physical controls are explicitly assumed.
- Only known preparation/control unitaries are reversed in the four-use
  algorithm. It never uses the inverse unknown gate.
- Independent cubic phases preserve the converse; fixed unknown uncorrected
  cubic error is not covered by the asymptotic upper bound. A theta-scaled
  higher term changes the generator and invalidates that automatic transfer.
- The Ising corollary uses fixed interacting N, unnormalized pair coupling,
  one uninterrupted fixed t, arbitrary input and final readout. It does not
  establish a Kerr-like four-query Ising threshold.
- General covariant optimization, finite-group query theory, number-theory
  representation/counting and fixed-point search are imported ingredients.
  Do not describe them as new general theorems of this project.
- Finite checks support their finite assertions. The general proofs and
  their attributions supply the universal and asymptotic conclusions.
